Seaborn:¶

Seaborn is a library for making statistical graphics in Python. It builds on top of matplotlib and integrates closely with pandas data structures. It provides:

  1. A high-level API for statistical graphics
  2. Statistical estimation
  3. Distributional representations
  4. Plots for categorical data
  5. Multivariate views on complex datasets
  6. Lower-level tools for building figures
  7. Opinionated defaults and flexible customization

Visualizing statistical relationships¶

In [9]:
#scatterplot using seaborn
sns.scatterplot(x=df.index, y = df['sepal_length'],data=df,hue=df['species'], style=df['species'])
Out[9]:
<Axes: xlabel='None', ylabel='sepal_length'>

Scatter plot using: relplot(): This is a figure-level function for visualizing statistical relationships using two common approaches: scatter plots and line plots

In [10]:
tips = sns.load_dataset("tips")
sns.relplot(data=tips, x="total_bill", y="tip", hue="smoker")
Out[10]:
<seaborn.axisgrid.FacetGrid at 0x28aa3a964b0>

Visualizing distributions of data¶

The axes-level functions are histplot(), kdeplot(). They are grouped together within the figure-level displot(), jointplot(), and pairplot() functions.

In [15]:
# Plotting univariate histograms
penguins = sns.load_dataset("penguins")
sns.displot(penguins, x="flipper_length_mm")
Out[15]:
<seaborn.axisgrid.FacetGrid at 0x28aa63f7410>
In [16]:
# Choosing the bin size
sns.displot(penguins, x="flipper_length_mm", binwidth=3)
Out[16]:
<seaborn.axisgrid.FacetGrid at 0x28aa640c740>
In [17]:
# Conditioning on other variables
sns.displot(penguins, x="flipper_length_mm", hue="species")    # element:step
Out[17]:
<seaborn.axisgrid.FacetGrid at 0x28aa6c5bad0>
In [18]:
# Normalized histogram statistics
# density
sns.displot(penguins, x="flipper_length_mm", hue="species", stat="density")
Out[18]:
<seaborn.axisgrid.FacetGrid at 0x28aa61d2480>
In [19]:
# probability
sns.displot(penguins, x="flipper_length_mm", hue="species", stat="probability")
Out[19]:
<seaborn.axisgrid.FacetGrid at 0x28aa60279e0>
In [20]:
# Kernel density estimation
sns.displot(penguins, x="flipper_length_mm", kind="kde")
Out[20]:
<seaborn.axisgrid.FacetGrid at 0x28aa61d2030>
In [21]:
sns.displot(penguins, x="flipper_length_mm", hue="species", kind="kde", multiple="stack")
Out[21]:
<seaborn.axisgrid.FacetGrid at 0x28aa7cbed80>
In [22]:
# Plotting many distributions
sns.pairplot(penguins)
Out[22]:
<seaborn.axisgrid.PairGrid at 0x28aa6cc3ef0>

Visualizing categorical data¶

Categorical scatterplots:

  1. stripplot() (with kind="strip"; the default)
  2. swarmplot() (with kind="swarm")

Categorical distribution plots:

  1. boxplot() (with kind="box")
  2. violinplot() (with kind="violin")
  3. boxenplot() (with kind="boxen")

Categorical estimate plots:

  1. pointplot() (with kind="point")
  2. barplot() (with kind="bar")
  3. countplot() (with kind="count")
In [23]:
# strip plot
tips = sns.load_dataset("tips")
sns.catplot(data=tips, x="day", y="total_bill")
